PM — Start the Termination Wizard
01
Property Address
Wizard Step 1 of 9
▾
Step 1 — Property Address panel

The wizard opens with the Termination Notice User Guide visible in the main panel. The right panel becomes the wizard interface, starting at Step 1 of 9.

Enter the property address using one of two methods:

  • Search Address — type the address into the search bar to look it up
  • Address Fields — expand the manual entry section and fill in: Unit No, Street No, Street Name, Street Type, Suburb, State, Postcode
ℹ
If the property address isn't returning a search result, use the manual Address Fields option instead.
Then click Next ›
02
Select Tenancy Agreement
Wizard Step 2 of 9 · Optional
▾
Step 2 — Select Tenancy Agreement list

Search for and select an existing FM00401 Residential Tenancy Agreement from the list. Selecting one auto-populates tenant and landlord details in Step 3.

The list shows form name, form number, the user who created it, and the date. Use the search bar to filter if you have many forms.

If no linked agreement exists: click Next without selecting anything. A Confirmation Required prompt will appear asking "Are you sure you want to skip this step?" — click Yes, Skip. You will need to enter party details manually in Step 3.
Then click Next › or Yes, Skip
03
Confirm Party Details
Wizard Step 3 of 9
▾
Step 3 — Party Details panel

Review and confirm landlord and tenant details. These will be pre-populated if you linked a tenancy agreement in Step 2.

Landlord Details

  • Option to tick Landlord Corporation / Government Department if applicable
  • Landlord 1: Name, Email, Phone (required)
  • Landlord 2 can be expanded and added if needed

Tenant Details

  • Select tenant type: Individual, Corporation, or Public Service Agency
  • Tenant 1: Name, Email, Phone (required)
  • Up to Tenant 4 can be added by expanding the additional tenant fields
ℹ
The Landlord Email entered here is where the Landlord Confirmation request will be sent in Step 6. Make sure it is current and correct.
Then click Next ›
04
Select Termination Reason
Wizard Step 4 of 9
▾
Step 5 — Termination Details (Landlord Moving In example)

Select the applicable termination ground. The ground you select determines what happens in Step 5 — different reasons have different required fields, documents, and supporting statements.

Common termination grounds include:

  • Landlord or Family Member Moving In
  • Sale of Property
  • Significant Renovations/Demolition
  • Change of Use
  • Breach of Agreement
  • End of Fixed Term
Important — Residential Tenancies Amendment Act 2024: Landlords are now required to provide reasons for termination. Selecting the correct ground is a legal requirement, not optional.
Then click Next ›
05
Enter Termination Details
Wizard Step 5 of 9 · Fields vary by reason
▾
Step 5 — Termination Details panel

Enter the details required for the selected termination reason. The fields shown depend on the ground selected in Step 4.

Example — Landlord or Family Member Moving In:

  • Termination Date — enter the date the tenancy is to end (DD/MM/YYYY)
  • Occupant Details — select who will be moving in: The Landlord or Landlord Family Member

Supporting Documents required for this ground:

Landlord Written Statement Family Member Written Statement (if applicable)
ℹ
The wizard highlights which supporting documents will be requested from the landlord in Step 6. These are shown in preview here so you know what to expect.
Termination date rules: For a periodic agreement, not earlier than 90 days after the date of service. For a short fixed term (6 months or less), on or after the end of the agreement and not earlier than 60 days after service. For another fixed term, on or after the end of the agreement and not earlier than 90 days after service.
Then click Next ›
06
Send Landlord Confirmation Request
Wizard Step 6 of 9 · Triggers landlord workflow
▾
Step 6 — Send Landlord Request panel

An Information & Signing Request is sent to the landlord. Review the following before sending:

  • Forms & Annexures that will be sent: Landlord Termination Confirmation + Landlord Written Statement
  • Recipient details — confirm the landlord's name, email, and phone are correct
  • Message field — a default message is pre-filled. You can customise it if needed
  • Supporting Documents listed below show what the landlord will be asked to provide
Once sent, the landlord receives an automated email from no-reply@reiformslive.com.au. The wizard will pause here until the landlord completes and signs their forms. Check the Forms list for status updates.
Then click Send Request ›
Landlord — Out-of-System Workflow
A
Landlord Receives the Email
Sent by REI Forms Live on behalf of the agent
▾
Landlord email from REI Forms Live

The landlord receives an email from no-reply@reiformslive.com.au with the subject line indicating a request from the agent's agency.

The email states: "[Agent Name] from [Agency] has requested some information."

The landlord clicks the green View Form button, which opens the REI Forms Live portal in their browser. No login is required.

ℹ
If the landlord can't find the email, ask them to check spam/junk folders. The sender domain is reiformslive.com.au. A URL is also included in the email in case the button doesn't work.
What happens next — before you continue to Step 7

Once the landlord request is sent, the Landlord Termination Confirmation form automatically separates from the Termination Wizard. It appears as its own form in the Forms tab with its own status — you can monitor whether the landlord has signed from there.

To continue the wizard: return to the FM00404 Termination Notice of a Residential Tenancy Agreement form in your Forms tab — it will show as Draft. Click it to re-enter the wizard and continue from Step 7.

The Landlord Statement shows as "Signed" — click the Termination Notice (FM00404) in Draft status to continue the wizard from Step 7.
B
Landlord Completes the Confirmation Form
Landlord Termination Confirmation + Written Statement
▾
Landlord Termination Confirmation form

The landlord lands on a branded REI Forms Live page and clicks Get Started to open the Landlord Termination Confirmation form:

  • If relevant, the landlord uploads any supporting documentation requested by the agent
  • Landlord(s), Tenant(s), Premises, and Agent details are pre-populated
  • The landlord reviews the form — if a written statement is included they complete the required fields and click Complete
  • If there is no written statement, the landlord simply reviews the form and clicks Complete to proceed to signing
The screenshot below shows the Written Statement view — this section only appears when the termination ground requires a written statement from the landlord.

Once the form is complete, the landlord clicks Complete in the top-right corner. A confirmation dialog asks them to confirm — they click Yes, Complete. The request is then locked and cannot be edited.

Landlord clicks Complete → then Yes, Complete
Written Statement section — mobile (left) and desktop (right)
C
Landlord Signs the Document
Forms Live Sign — electronic signature
▾
Forms Live Sign — signature panel

After completing the form, the landlord is automatically redirected to Forms Live Sign (in 3 seconds, or via the link in the confirmation dialog).

A signing intro pop-up appears confirming the request. The landlord clicks Get Started.

The document is displayed. The landlord:

  • Clicks the Start tab on the left and scrolls to the signature field
  • Clicks Sign Here
  • A signature dialog appears — choose Standard (auto-generated from name) or Draw
  • Enters full name, previews the signature, then clicks Adopt Signature
  • A "Nearly Finished..." dialog confirms all fields are complete
  • Clicks Complete to finalise
Once the landlord signs and completes, the Signing Status page confirms "Document Signing Complete." The landlord can download a copy. Back in the Forms list, the Landlord Statement status changes to Signed.
PM — Back to the Wizard
Before you continue — return to the Termination Wizard

Once the Landlord Request is sent, the Landlord Termination Confirmation form automatically separates from the wizard. It appears as its own form in the Forms tab with its own status — you can monitor whether the landlord has signed from there.

To continue: go back to the Forms tab and open the FM00404 Termination Notice of a Residential Tenancy Agreement form — it will show as Draft. Click it to re-enter the wizard and continue from Step 7.

The Landlord Statement (Signed) and the FM00404 Termination Notice (Draft) — click the Draft form to continue the wizard.
07
Review Landlord Documents
Wizard Step 7 of 9 · Confirm before proceeding
▾
Step 7 — Review Landlord Documents

Return to the Termination Notice in REI Forms Live. The wizard will now show Step 7 of 9 — Review: Landlord Documents.

Confirm that the required landlord documents have been received and signed:

Landlord Termination Confirmation Landlord Written Statement

Use the View and Download links next to each document to review the content before proceeding.

Important: The system notes that "the landlord provided documents and information must meet the termination notice requirements." Review the content carefully — an incomplete or vague Written Statement may invalidate the notice. You can upload additional files on the next step if needed.
Then click Next ›
08
Enter Notice Details
Wizard Step 8 of 9 · Service method and date
▾
Step 8 — Notice Details panel

Two sections to complete on this step:

Additional Documents — upload any extra files or evidence relevant to the termination notice using the Upload Files button.

Service Details

Notice Service Date Enter the date the notice will be (or was) served — DD/MM/YYYY Service of Notice Select how the notice will be served

Service method options:

  • Serve in person — handing it to the tenant directly
  • Serve via mail — mailing it (allow 7 working days for service)
  • Serve via letterbox — placing it in an envelope in the tenant's letterbox
  • Serve on person at the premises — handing it to someone 16+ at the premises
  • Serve via last known address — if tenant can't otherwise be reached
  • Serve via email — requires tenant's consent; enter tenant's email address
Postal service: Not less than 7 working days must be allowed for postal delivery. The days between the date of posting and the estimated delivery date (inclusive) must not be counted when calculating the notice period.
Then click Next ›
09
Review and Complete the Wizard
Wizard Step 9 of 9 · Final confirmation
▾
Step 9 — Review / Complete summary

Review the full summary before completing the wizard. Check each section carefully:

  • Address — property address as entered
  • Termination Details — all landlord documents listed with ticks and View/Download links
  • Summary — Termination Reason, Termination Date, Notice Method, Delivery Email, Notice Delivery date
  • Tenant Details and Landlord Details — expandable for review
Once you click Complete, the wizard is marked as complete and the form enters draft status. A yellow advisory note reminds you to review, finalise, sign and serve as per instructions.
Then click Complete ›
10
Sign, Finalise and Serve
PM completes their signatures, then downloads and serves
▾
Step 10 — Signed form with agent signature

With the wizard complete, you are now in the full form view. The toolbar shows: Finalise, Share, Download, Mappings, Prefill, History, More. A yellow note reminds you to review, finalise, sign and serve.

1. Sign the Termination Notice
  • Scroll to the bottom of the Termination Notice form
  • The Signature of Landlord/Agent field is highlighted in yellow
  • Click the field — a Sign Form dialog appears with your user name pre-selected
  • Draw your signature in the box, then click Save
  • Your signature, printed name, and the date auto-populate
2. Sign the Service of Notice section
  • Scroll further to the Service of Notice section
  • The Signature of person serving notice field also needs to be signed using the same process
3. Finalise
  • Click Finalise in the toolbar
  • The form enters finalised status. The Annexures tab shows all attached supporting documents (Landlord Termination Confirmation, Written Statement) as a complete package
4. Download and Serve
  • Click Download in the toolbar to save the full package as a PDF
  • A Print Options dialog appears — the Attach Files option includes the Written Statement PDF. Tick this to include it
  • Click Print to generate the complete print-ready set
The final downloaded document includes the completed Termination Notice plus the NSW Fair Trading Termination Information Statement, which must be given to the tenant alongside the notice. Serve on the tenant by the method selected in Step 8.
ℹ
After serving: Record the service date and method in your file notes. If serving by post, note the posting date and calculate the 7 working day addition to confirm the effective service date.
Landlord Workflow (PM reference) — Select the workflow that applies. Your property manager will have let you know which one to follow.
You may have received a link by SMS or email. Both open the same form — the steps are identical on phone or computer.

Open the link from your SMS or email

Workflow with an Upload Request
You may be asked to upload supporting documents (e.g. a copy of the contract for sale). Your property manager may handle this for you instead — they will let you know. If so, just click Close when the upload prompt appears.
1
Open the link from your SMS or email
From: REI Forms Live · no-reply@reiformslive.com.au
▾
SMS link (left) and email (right) — both open the same form

Tap or click the link. No login required.

Can't find the email? Check spam/junk. Sender is reiformslive.com.au. Use the SMS link if you have it.

Click Get Started
REI Forms Live welcome page

Welcome page — mobile (left) and desktop (right)

This is where the two paths differ
▾
Upload Documents dialog — Choose File and Upload, OR click Close, mobile (left) and desktop (right)

An Upload Documents dialog appears immediately listing the documents requested (e.g. Copy of Contract, Solicitor/Conveyancer Statement).

ℹ
If your property manager asked you to upload: Click Choose File, select the file, name it, then click Upload. Wait for confirmation before continuing.

If your property manager said they will handle it: Click Close. They will upload the required documents at a later stage.
Not sure which applies? Contact your property manager before proceeding.
